name: Berlin
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Berlin: start-up and investor due diligence, insolvency and asset research and public-sector risk inquiries.
hero_lede: Investigative consulting for matters connected to Berlin: due diligence on start-ups, founders and investors in Germany's leading venture capital hub, research around insolvencies and real estate holdings, and integrity questions near the federal government. Scoped from Nashville with qualified German professionals and counsel.
intro: Berlin is Germany's capital and largest city, a city-state with 3,685,265 residents at the end of 2024, 22.5 percent of them without German citizenship, according to the Statistical Office for Berlin-Brandenburg. It is the seat of the federal government, the Bundestag and the Bundesrat, and hosts embassies of 159 countries. The State of Berlin reports economic output of 218.3 billion euros in 2025 and growth well above the national rate, driven by services. Berlin is Germany's leading start-up centre: the state says 32 percent of German venture capital invested in 2025 went to Berlin start-ups and that 52 of the country's top 100 start-ups are based there. Science City Adlershof, Germany's largest science and technology park, anchors its research economy.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Berlin because capital, policy and new companies meet there. Typical triggers include due diligence on start-ups, founders and co-investors before venture or growth rounds and acquisitions; background research on executives in fintech, software and digital health; asset and ownership research in real estate, where holdings are often structured through layered companies; support to creditors and counsel in insolvencies administered by the city's central insolvency court; and integrity research on consultants, lobbyists and contractors in matters touching federal ministries, agencies or the state's public enterprises. Embassy and diplomatic presence also brings politically exposed person questions into commercial work.

matters.title: Start-up and founder due diligence
matters.text: Background research on Berlin start-ups, founders, co-investors and key employees before seed, growth or acquisition transactions, covering commercial register history, prior ventures and insolvencies, litigation, conflicting interests and reputation, to test the claims made in pitch materials and data rooms.

matters.title: Fintech and digital business checks
matters.text: Ownership, management and regulatory history of Berlin payment, lending, crypto-asset and software companies, drawing on register filings, published supervisory notices and open sources, to support partnerships, investments, banking relationships, payment-processing arrangements and outsourcing decisions by counterparties.

matters.title: Insolvency and creditor support
matters.text: Research supporting creditors, investors and counsel when Berlin companies fail, including chronologies of transfers before insolvency, related-party links, successor businesses and assets held by directors or shareholders, aligned with proceedings administered by the Local Court Charlottenburg as central insolvency court.

matters.title: Real estate ownership research
matters.text: Identification of the companies, funds and individuals behind Berlin residential and commercial property holdings, mapping layered ownership structures through register filings and public records, for buyers, lenders, tenants' counsel and parties investigating disputed or suspicious transactions.

matters.title: Public-sector and lobbying integrity
matters.text: Lawful research on consultants, lobbyists, contractors and intermediaries connected to federal ministries, agencies or Berlin state enterprises, identifying conflicts of interest, undisclosed relationships and politically exposed persons, to support compliance reviews, procurement disputes and internal investigations.

local_context.title: Local Court Charlottenburg registers
local_context.text: The Local Court Charlottenburg keeps Berlin's commercial register, cooperative, partnership and association registers and the matrimonial property register. It is also the city's central insolvency court, handling insolvency proceedings across Berlin except consumer insolvencies, which go to the court where the debtor lives. Register entries are searchable through the joint register portal of the German states described on the Germany country page, and insolvency publications are a core source in Berlin research.

local_context.title: Berlin courts
local_context.text: Berlin's civil courts are organised under the Kammergericht, the city-state's higher regional court and one of Germany's oldest courts, with first-instance commercial cases going to the Berlin regional courts. As a city-state, Berlin has a single court hierarchy and justice administration. Whether Berlin has established a specialised English-language commercial court under the 2024 federal act should be checked with counsel at the time of a dispute.

local_context.title: Berlin data protection supervision
local_context.text: Germany's federal data protection rules apply nationwide, but most private-sector processing is supervised by the state authorities. For organisations established in Berlin this is the Berlin Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information. Investigative work involving employees, customers or users of Berlin companies, including start-ups processing large volumes of personal data, should be planned with the data protection officer, works council arrangements and that authority's guidance in mind.

local_context.title: Federal institutions and public enterprises
local_context.text: As seat of the federal government and parliament, Berlin hosts federal ministries and agencies, and the Bundestag's lobby register is a public source on interest representation. The State of Berlin also owns 61 companies, including its development bank IBB, transport operator BVG, housing companies and the water utility, which are frequent counterparties in procurement, construction, housing and service contracting with private companies.

tdsc_approach: For matters touching Berlin, TDSC first separates the commercial question, such as an investment or insolvency, from any public-sector dimension, because Berlin work often involves federal bodies, state-owned companies or politically exposed persons. Research uses the commercial register and insolvency publications kept through the Local Court Charlottenburg, published financial statements, court records, public lobbying and procurement information and open sources, reviewed under the GDPR and German data protection law. Start-up due diligence is calibrated to the stage of the company and the claims under test. Where interviews or local inquiries in Berlin are needed, TDSC coordinates qualified German investigators operating under the applicable trade rules and German counsel. TDSC has no office in Berlin.

faqs.q: What does start-up due diligence in Berlin typically cover?
faqs.a: TDSC reviews register history, shareholdings and prior companies of the founders, insolvency and court records, conflicts of interest, sanctions exposure and media coverage, and tests key claims about customers, partners or technology against public sources. The depth is set by the size of the investment and the risks the investor wants to resolve.

faqs.q: Where are Berlin company and insolvency records kept?
faqs.a: Berlin's commercial register is kept by the Local Court Charlottenburg, which is also the central insolvency court for the city except for consumer insolvencies. Register entries and filed documents are available through the joint register portal of the German states, and insolvency notices are published online, both of which TDSC uses as primary sources.

faqs.q: Can TDSC research consultants or lobbyists linked to federal ministries?
faqs.a: Yes, through lawful sources. TDSC uses public registers, including the Bundestag lobby register, corporate filings, procurement notices, court records and media to identify relationships and conflicts. It does not access confidential government files or use pretexting, and it reports facts for the client and counsel to assess.

faqs.q: Which data protection authority is relevant for a Berlin company?
faqs.a: Private-sector processing by organisations established in Berlin is generally supervised by the Berlin Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information. TDSC plans any research involving employees or users with the client's counsel and data protection officer and limits the personal data gathered to what the agreed purpose requires.

faqs.q: Does TDSC have staff in Berlin?
faqs.a: No. TDSC has no office, staff or address in Berlin or elsewhere in Germany. Engagements are scoped and managed from Nashville, Tennessee. Where a matter requires local inquiries, TDSC coordinates independent German investigators and works with the client's German counsel under a written scope agreed in advance.
